component.name: Card
component.description: Base container for decision-oriented content. Groups title, optional visual, chip, description, metadata, and CTA into one scannable unit.

antiPatterns.reason: A button communicates action with less visual weight.
Cards reduce scan speed for urgent tasks.
Cards are item containers, not system messages.

contentRules: Title is the main decision cue and should fit in one or two lines.
Subtitle explains context or consequence, max two lines.
Metadata is secondary: date, status, or progress summary.
Chip is optional and translates priority into human language.
Navigation card must not use internal **buttons**; use the whole card as the single action.
When `href` is set with `ctaType=link` and the same destination, the card renders as one `<a>` and the link label is decorative (no nested interactive control).
Use internal CTAs only when there are two distinct actions; render primary + secondary Button (sm).
Internal link CTA is optional for secondary emphasis when the card is not the sole navigation target.

rules: DS Health: no aparece en la tabla de paridad `component/…` porque los estilos usan solo tokens globales (semantic, typography, space, radius, etc.).
Reuse Chip / Priority for status or priority; do not draw chip geometry locally.
Reuse Button (primary + secondary, sm) when ctaType=buttons.
Use Icon / Action for icon visuals.

Image visual is full-bleed on vertical **default** cards: it reaches the card edges and only the content body keeps inner padding; `surface=editorial` keeps padding 0 on the root, uses normal image insets, and rounds the image on all four corners with no card border or fill.
Optional `contentCategoryLabel` renders an editorial overline (not Chip / Priority); tone maps to semantic status colors for discovery modules.
CardCarousel composes Card instances; Card remains usable standalone.
Optional `children` render below metadata/CTA inside the body grid (e.g. embed an ActionList for a task summary card).

layout.behavior: Whole card is the hit target for navigation only when there is no internal CTA. Pair of buttons implies two actions and disables whole-card navigation.

accessibility.role: article, link, or button depending on interaction
accessibility.keyboardSupport: Clickable card receives one focus target; internal CTA receives independent focus when it is a real button (not when the whole card is already an anchor with a decorative link label).
accessibility.screenReader: Reading order follows the Figma documentation annotations: optional visual/chip context, title as accessible name, subtitle, metadata, and CTA if present. Whole-card links with decorative CTA text use `aria-label` on the anchor combining title and CTA.
accessibility.focusManagement: Navigation card without internal CTA has one focus target. Two buttons receive separate tab stops; the card surface does not. Internal link CTA is a separate button unless merged into a single anchor with decorative link text.

aiHints.context: Use Card when the user must understand or choose one item. Use CardCarousel only for exploratory groups.
